category.infestusfrontier.contact.name: First Contact
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.the_wakin: This guide covers the starting ingredients and how the colony grows only where you choose. Each page names what you need first. Nothing here is required to play. Read a page when you want to know what to do next. Picking up a log opens the Infestus Frontier tab of the Advancements screen (L): it lists the first steps, from a Spore Culture to a working biomass workshop.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.organ_bud: A blank that grows into an organ
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.surgical_: Organs are hard to break: about 18 seconds with a hand or any ordinary tool, so a stray click never takes one. A broken organ comes out whole, with everything it holds and every batch it has done, ready to place again. The Surgical Blade cuts an organ out in a second and a half and lasts 64 uses, worn by anything it breaks. Grown tissue is different: veins, Mouths and beds never move, and a broken cell dies into Dead Tissue.
An iron ingot, a bone and a Membrane Sheet make the blade.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.speak_to_: Read an organ without opening it
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.a_culture: Rotten flesh, a red mushroom and wheat seeds.
Use Spore Culture on exposed dirt, grass, mud or stone to turn it into basic Living Substrate. Lost this book? Craft it again from a book and one Spore Culture.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.living_su: Bone meal grows a cell. The fed cell matures and converts the ground beside it: a mature core, a young ring, a basic edge. Bone meal the edge to grow on. Cells never spread on their own. Grown tissue never moves: a broken cell dies into Dead Tissue, whatever the tool, and so does everything grown in a cell.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.living_wa: Walls are grown, never placed. Sneak and use bone meal on a mature cell: a Living Wall grows on it. Bone meal on the top of a wall grows it one block higher, one block a bone meal. Like every grown cell, a broken wall dies into Dead Tissue, and no piston moves it.

Grafts harden a wall one block at a time. A Skeletal Graft turns a Living Wall into a Ribbed Wall, tougher than stone. A Calcifying Graft turns a Ribbed Wall into a Calcified Wall, which no explosion breaks; a pickaxe takes it down fastest. The Activation Cyst makes both grafts.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.withered_: What growth leaves of the undergrowth

Living Substrate growing under a shrub, grass or sapling kills it. Spore Culture on the ground under a sweet berry bush, dead bush, short grass, fern or an oak, birch, spruce, jungle, acacia or dark oak sapling, or a bone-meal wave reaching that ground, leaves a Dead Berry Bush, Blighted Dead Bush, Blighted Undergrowth or Withered Sapling where the plant stood: bare twigs, dry blades or a curled frond, in ash, brown, straw or plum. Nothing drops and nothing grows.

Each keeps only what its harvest needs: a sapling its species, grass or fern which it was, a berry bush its age. Break one, or the cell under it, and the plant drops once, as the living one would for your tool: shears give a dead bush, short grass or fern itself, bare hands sticks or now and then a seed, and a sapling comes back as the same sapling. Pick block gives the plant.

A Dead Berry Bush drops what its age would have given: nothing at age 0 or 1, one or two berries at age 2, two or three at age 3, more with Fortune. It cannot be picked, hurts nothing and never bears again. A Withered Sapling never grows a tree. Bone meal does nothing to any of them. Crops, torchflowers, azaleas, mushrooms, potted and water plants and plants from other mods keep their ground and stay alive. See Withered Flowers for flowers and tall plants.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.infected_: A living oak, the same oak infected and Infected Logs cut from it.

An infected tree keeps its shape. Its trunk becomes Infected Log, charcoal bark split by pale bone ribs and dark sealed clefts, dull maroon tissue here and there, and its crown Blighted Leaves, hooked dry twigs and torn membrane in a mostly empty block, so sky and branches show through. They are the same two blocks whatever the tree was: oak, cherry or a tree another mod adds. A standing tree becomes them when Living Substrate reaches the foot of its trunk. No recipe makes a log from nothing.

Grow substrate to the trunk: a bone-meal wave that reaches the ground beside the lowest log, or Spore Culture on that ground, touches the tree. The colony then finds the tree, log by log, and turns it: the logs first, from the foot up, then the leaves, sixteen blocks a tick. Nothing drops and no experience falls; cocoa pods on a jungle trunk, which cannot hang on an Infected Log, vanish with their log and drop nothing. The ground under the trunk stays as it is; touching the trunk is enough.

A tree is an upright trunk log standing on dirt, grass, stone or any other host, or on a cell; every log of that same block joined to it through a face, an edge or a corner; and the leaves those logs hold, by their leaf distance, of the kinds that touch the trunk. A trunk log is a natural log, oak to cherry and the trees of other mods. Stripped logs, wood blocks, mangroves, thin branches, logs with contents, planks, fences, chests and mechanisms are never part of it and stay. A built stack of logs and leaves counts too. Leaves never lead into the next tree: where crowns touch, each tree keeps its own.

A tree is refused and left whole when it has more than 128 logs or 512 leaves, reaches past 8 blocks from the trunk or 32 up, needs more than 2,048 looks, joins a log of another kind, holds more than four kinds of leaves, or stands partly in unloaded land. A world works on 16 trees at once; a seventeenth is refused and the wave converts the ground as usual. Every refusal shows above the hotbar. A tree touched twice is one job. A job waits while its chunk is unloaded, survives a save and finishes after. A block you change meanwhile is left as you left it. Infected Logs never start another infection.

Cut an Infected Log with an axe or anything else and it drops one Infected Log, never the original log as well, whatever the tree was. Put it down and cut it again: still one. Build with it, or burn it as you would a log. Its one recipe is the Capsule Stem, on the next page. No recipe makes planks from it; Infected Planks an older world still holds work as planks, and they make no stem. It is not Living Wood: no sap, no resin, no extra biomass, and no treatment turns it into anything.

Storage Tree: turn a tree with substrate, cut its Infected Log, and at a crafting table combine it with a chest, two Membrane Sheets and a Spore Culture for one Capsule Stem. Any tree's log serves. An oak log, any other ordinary log or an old Infected Plank is refused. Stems already grown, and what their pods hold, are unchanged.

Blighted Leaves keep their leaf distance, whether a player placed them, and water. A log of any kind keeps them standing; cut the trunk and they decay as vanilla leaves do. Broken or decayed they drop nothing: no sapling, stick, apple or fruit of the tree they were. Shears or Silk Touch give Blighted Leaves, the same for every tree, to place as dead foliage. They have no production.

Infected timber makes nothing by itself: no resin, no fruit, no regrowth and no spread. Ordinary planks and stripped logs are not infected timber. In the demo, the Timber plot sets six living trees beside the log and crown each becomes. The Woodland plot has an oak to turn with a button or bone meal, touching crowns, a treehouse, a giant spruce too large to take and supplies with a crafting table. The Grove sets a living grove beside the same grove infected: a 2x2 trunk, lying branches, low foliage and a frame built of Infected Logs.

Which trees count is data. A trunk is a log in the block tag infestusfrontier:infectable_logs, by default vanilla's minecraft:overworld_natural_logs, and not in infestusfrontier:uninfectable_logs or the common stripped log and wood tags. Foliage is leaves in infestusfrontier:infectable_leaves, by default minecraft:leaves, and not in infestusfrontier:uninfectable_leaves. A data pack adds or removes a tree there; no list of species is kept anywhere.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.withered_: What growth leaves of a meadow

Living Substrate growing under a small flower kills it. Spore Culture on the ground under a dandelion, poppy, blue orchid, allium, azure bluet, tulip, oxeye daisy, cornflower or lily of the valley, or a bone-meal wave reaching that ground, leaves a Withered Flower where the flower stood: a bent stalk with a spent head, a forked stalk with dry pods, or a collapsed bloom, in ash, bone, brown or plum. Nothing drops and nothing grows.

A Withered Flower is dead ground cover. It keeps only the name of the flower it was: break it, or break the cell under it, and that flower drops once, as it would from the living plant. Pick block gives the flower too. Bone meal or culture on a dead flower does nothing. It burns like a flower.

Tall plants wither whole. Culture, or a bone-meal wave, on the ground under a sunflower, lilac, rose bush, peony, tall grass or large fern leaves a Tall Withered Flower or Tall Blighted Undergrowth over both blocks: a dry stalk with spent heads, dry blades or curled fronds, in ash, bone, brown, plum or straw. Break either half, or the cell under it, and the plant drops once, as the living one would: the flower itself, or from grass and fern two short plants with shears and now and then a seed. Pick block gives the plant. Nothing grows.

Growth takes only ground it can account for. Ground under a crop, a torchflower, an azalea, a mushroom, sugar cane, bamboo, a dripleaf or any other rooted plant without a dead form stays as it is, and the plant stays with it. So does ground under a tall plant that is not whole (a lone lower half or a mismatched pair) and under a pitcher plant. Dormant cells never attack a plant planted later; only a new treatment does. Shrubs, short grass, ferns and saplings wither the same way: see Withered Shrubs.
A wall opens by mutation. Use a Membrane Window on a wall cell of any tier: it turns to veined, translucent membrane in a bone frame, and windows side by side join into one pane. Use a Sphincter Door on a wall cell with another wall cell above or below it: the two become a doorway whose membrane flaps draw back into the rim, by hand or by redstone. A Sphincter Door is a simple door: villagers open it, and zombies can break it down. A Skeletal Graft on it grows bone ribs into a Clenched Door, which opens only by redstone, like an iron door, so put a button or lever beside it; no mob opens or breaks it. A Calcifying Graft then plates it into a Calcified Door, which no explosion breaks; like any door it stands on the block below, so give it a floor as hard. Broken, every opening dies into Dead Tissue.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.leaching_: Weaken soft ground so a pit digs by hand

Grow it from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate. Its growth pays for all 16 of its charges, and it cannot be picked up again: a broken pod leaves nothing. Once a second it turns one layer of ground below it, a disc seven blocks across, into Leached Rock. The first layer includes the substrate it stands on. A layer that changes at least one block costs a charge; the pod never works more than 16 layers down. Right-click it to read its progress. Unloaded chunks pause it, and a reload or a restart resumes it where it was. Only finishing its layers or charges spends it, and the husk stays.

Dirt, sand, gravel, sandstone, stone, granite, diorite, andesite, tuff, netherrack, basalt, blackstone and Living Substrate, when no harder than stone. Deepslate, ores, fluids, anything with an inventory and every other block stay as they are, so a pod is no use deep down.

Translucent and solid, with a faint glow in some blocks. It breaks almost at once by hand and drops nothing, and no fluid moves until you break it. Dig the pit with bare hands and every ore in it shows before you reach it.
Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply four rotten flesh, four bone meal and a spider eye.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.tunnel_ro: Drive a level tunnel one step at a time

Grow it from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate; it faces away from you. It cuts a tunnel one block wide and two high. Feed it by hand: right-click with Root Segments (it holds 16) and with a Biomass Bucket (it holds two buckets). Any other hand opens its screen. Nothing reaches it through veins, hoppers or pipes. Break it with the Surgical Blade and it comes out whole, with what it holds and the cells it has laid.

Every 20 seconds the head cuts the two blocks in front of it, as a stone pickaxe would, and drops what they would drop into its output, once. It turns one Root Segment into a Root Cell in the floor under the cut, pays 25 BU of biomass and moves forward one block. The root runs the length of the tunnel; a root has at most 64 cells. Walk the tunnel behind it and take the drops from its screen.

The button on the screen sets the next step: straight, left or right. A turned step cuts a quarter turn to that side, so the tunnel stays level and follows the four directions; the cell where it turned shows the bend. After the turn the head goes straight again.

The screen names the reason: no segment or not enough biomass; a full output (one stack in all); a block harder than stone grade, or one with an inventory; fluid in or next to the cut; no plain ground under the cut; sand, gravel or another loose block on top of the cut; ground ahead that is not loaded; the head off its root; or a root at 64 cells.

Fix the cause and the head carries on with the same step: load segments or biomass, take the drops out, mine the hard block or the loose block by hand, drain or block the fluid, place cobblestone or dirt where the floor is missing, or come back so the ground loads. Nothing is lost while it waits: its supplies, its drops and its progress stay, through unloading, saving and restarting.
Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply four bones, four rotten flesh and a stone pickaxe.
Four Root Segments from a Bone Plate, a rotten flesh and a stick.
Gather DNA samples and complete a genome

Research starts with DNA. Take samples from pigs with a Sampling Needle, and craft a DNA Bank from an Organ Bud and place it on Living Substrate. Give the bank samples and biomass: it extracts them one at a time and adds each to the pig genome until the genome is complete. The bank keeps the complete genome.

Right-click a living pig with the Sampling Needle to take one Pig DNA Sample. The pig is not hurt. Each sample wears the needle by one, 64 in all, and the needle rests a second between samples. If your inventory has no room, or the creature gives no DNA, the needle says so and takes nothing. So far only pigs give DNA.

Right-click the bank with samples to load them; it holds 16. A hopper can feed it too, but nothing takes samples back out except you, at its screen. Biomass arrives by Biomass Bucket, vein or pipe; it holds two buckets. Each pig sample takes 5 seconds and 100 BU and adds 10% to the pig genome. The sample and the biomass are used when an extraction starts. The screen shows the extraction under way and each genome's progress.

Break the bank with the Surgical Blade and it comes out whole, with its samples, biomass, research and the extraction under way; its tooltip lists its genomes. Placed again, it carries on. Saving, unloading and restarting keep everything, and an unloaded bank simply pauses. A complete genome stays complete. One bank researches up to four species.

The screen names the reason: no Living Substrate under the bank; too little biomass for the next sample; an item in the slot that no recipe reads; a genome already complete; or a bank already researching four other species. The bank takes no more samples of a complete genome or of a fifth species, and those already in its slot stay there for you to take out.
The needle from an iron nugget, a bone and a glass bottle; the bank from an Organ Bud, two glass bottles, a Membrane Sheet and a Bone Plate.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.genetic_c: Turn a complete genome into a mutation

A complete genome is a recipe book, not a single use. A DNA Bank that holds a complete genome turns materials and biomass into a genetic construct: the physical material of one mutation. Put the materials in the three slots on the bank’s second row, in any order, and press Produce. The line under them names the construct they make, or why they make none.

Each press makes one construct, uses each material and the biomass once, and puts the construct in the slot beside the materials. The genome stays complete, so the bank makes more from new materials. Nothing is used when a genome the construct needs is not complete, the materials are wrong or mixed with anything else, the biomass is short, or the construct slot is full. Constructs and materials stay in the bank through breaking, unloading and restarting.

Right-click a Tunnel Root head with a Stairs Construct. The head pays 500 BU from its own tank, takes the construct, and becomes a Descending Rootstock for good. It keeps its segments, drops, cells and steward. Stairs permits a descending staircase; it brings no jaw, grower, segment or tread. Set before Surveyed Tissue with its organs around it, the Rootstock runs a staircase mine; anywhere else it still cuts level steps by hand. Its screen and its item name its mutations.

A Wider Section Construct goes on a Rootstock only, for 1000 BU from its tank. It lets the Rootstock's gallery faces cut wide routes, 3x3 instead of 1x2; the three jaws, the stock and the extra biomass that section needs are still yours to supply.

A construct is never used up for nothing. A head that already has the mutation, a plain head offered Wider Section, a head off its root or one with too little biomass refuses and names the reason; any other block takes nothing. A mutation is permanent: nothing removes it.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.organ_bud: Spore Culture, two rotten flesh and bone meal.

Place a Bud on Living Substrate. Right-click it with an empty hand to see which organ it will grow and what it still needs. Sneak with an empty hand to choose another organ, until you have supplied something. Right-click it holding the materials: it takes what the growth needs, and the organ grows in place when the last one is in. A Bud on ground that is no longer Living Substrate waits and loses nothing. Breaking a Bud gives back everything it was supplied. A Digestive Sac, a Biomass Bladder, a Culture Bowl, a Membrane Rack, a Bone Loom, a Bio-Furnace, an Awakening Cradle and a Leaching Pod grow this way; none is crafted. String picks the Rack, bones the Loom, a furnace the Bio-Furnace, a Bone Plate the Cradle and a spider eye the Pod; sticks and Membrane Sheets go to the one the Bud has chosen. The last two need what the Rack and the Loom make. The Culture Bowl also grows more Buds in batches.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.digestive: Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply two rotten flesh and a bowl.

Place it on Living Substrate. Feed it by hand or by hopper: wheat gives 100 BU in 2 seconds, rotten flesh 50 BU in 8, Dead Tissue 5 BU in 4. An empty bucket takes 1000 BU. Any other item opens the screen. A full Sac waits. Food a Mouth delivers through Item Veins counts as automatic work of the Sac's steward.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.biomass_b: Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply two glass and a slime ball.
Holds 4000 BU. A biomass bucket pours in, an empty bucket takes out. A Sac beside it fills it on its own. Any other item opens the screen.
An empty bucket on a Sac or a Bladder takes 1000 BU. Use the full bucket on a Bladder or a Bowl to pour it in. One BU is one mB.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.culture_b: Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply a flower pot, a Spore Culture and wheat seeds.

Place it on Living Substrate. Put ingredients in one at a time, or let a hopper load it, and pour water from a bucket. A batch starts on its own when the ingredients are complete and takes 60 seconds; spare ingredients wait for the next. Any other item opens the screen. Sneak with both hands empty to take a stack back.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.speak_to_: A bone, a slime ball and Spore Culture.

Use the Probe on an organ to read its biomass without opening the screen. Any other item, or an empty hand, opens the screen: what the organ holds and how far its work has come. Sneak to build against an organ.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.membrane_: Place it on Living Substrate. Put in rotten flesh or leather and string, by hand or by hopper, and pour water from a bucket. It starts on its own. A sheet takes 20 seconds from flesh, 40 from leather. Any other item opens the screen. Sneak with both hands empty to take a stack back.
Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply four string and two sticks.
gui.infestusfrontier.stage.story: %s more batches to the next stage
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.bio_furna: Smelt with biomass; it grows with use

Place it on Living Substrate. Put in anything a furnace smelts, by hand or by hopper, and a bucket of biomass. It starts on its own: 40 BU and 16 seconds per item, the normal result. Any other item opens the screen. The smelting experience waits in the furnace, up to 1000 points, for whoever takes the result. It also smelts dust: four dust of one metal make an ingot (see the Mineral Gizzard).

Every batch it completes counts. At 64 the furnace reaches its second stage and smelts in 12 seconds; at 512 its third, in 8. The body grows ridges, then lobes and chimneys. The count travels with the furnace when it is broken and placed again.
Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply a furnace and two Membrane Sheets. Give the furnace first, or sneak with an empty hand to choose it.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.bone_loom: Place it on Living Substrate. Put in bones, by hand or by hopper, and a bucket of biomass. It starts on its own. A plate takes 20 seconds and 50 BU. Biomass binds the bone; it does not make it. Any other item opens the screen. Sneak with both hands empty to take a stack back.
Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply two bones and two sticks.
item.infestusfrontier.living_tool.mutati: Contractile: breaks the 3×3 round each block it mines, 2 BU each
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.living_to: Bone tools that wake and mend

Bone Plates on sticks, in the shape of a pickaxe, axe, shovel or hoe, make a dormant tool. It digs what a wooden tool digs, only slower, and breaks after 12 blocks; an anvil mends it with Bone Plates. The Cradle wakes it, as it wakes a piece of armor: a Spore Culture and 100 BU, thirty seconds, as worn as it went in.
Three plates over a stick for a pick; two and one beside the stick for a hatchet; one for a spade; two for a hoe.

A living tool lasts 256 blocks and carries 40 BU, filled at a Biomass Bladder. While you carry it, it mends four points of wear a second, one BU each, until the reserve is dry. No material repairs it on an anvil.

A living pick, hatchet or spade with a Contractile Fiber and 200 BU in the Cradle takes its one branch. Each block it mines, it also breaks the eight round it on the face you struck, those it is the right tool for, as if you had broken them yourself, for 2 BU each from its reserve. Dry, it mines one block at a time. The branch is permanent and the tool keeps its wear and reserve. The Cradle refuses a tool that already has it: it takes neither the tool nor the fiber, and spends no biomass.
item.infestusfrontier.living_tool.mutati: Grasping: a hit grips its target, Slowness II for three seconds, 2 BU each
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.living_fa: A bone blade that wakes and grips

Two Bone Plates on a stick make a Dormant Fang: a weak blade, softer than a wooden sword, 12 strikes, mended with Bone Plates on an anvil. The Cradle wakes it as it wakes a tool: a Spore Culture and 100 BU, thirty seconds, as worn as it went in. A Living Fang bites a little harder, lasts 256 strikes, carries 40 BU filled at a Biomass Bladder, and mends itself from them while you carry it.

A Living Fang with a Contractile Fiber and 200 BU in the Cradle takes its one branch. Each hit grips: the target is slowed, Slowness II for three seconds, for 2 BU from the reserve. Dry, it only cuts. The branch is permanent and the fang keeps its wear and reserve. The Cradle refuses a fang that already has it: it takes neither the fang nor the fiber, and spends no biomass.
death.attack.infestusfrontier.spine: %1$s was lashed by a Spine Sentry
death.attack.infestusfrontier.spine.play: %1$s was lashed by a Spine Sentry while fighting %2$s
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.spine: A rooted lash that guards the colony

Place it on Living Substrate and feed it biomass by bucket or vein. Every second it lashes the nearest hostile it can see within six blocks and three up or down, three hearts a strike, for 10 BU. Players, villagers and animals are never struck. Dry, it rests; biomass arriving wakes it.

What a creature it kills drops goes into its eight wells before it can fall; only what does not fit falls. A hopper, a Mouth set to output or a Yield Lobe takes the wells; nothing fills them. With no room left in its wells it rests until items are taken out.
An Organ Bud, a crossbow and two Bone Plates.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.dormant_p: Craft rotten flesh in armor shapes. Dormant pieces have lower protection, durability, and enchantability than leather. Toughness and knockback resistance are both zero, matching leather. They hold nothing. The Cradle wakes them.
entry.infestusfrontier.contact.awakening: Place it on Living Substrate. Put in a dormant piece, a Spore Culture and a bucket of biomass. It starts on its own. Thirty seconds and 100 BU later the piece is awake, as worn as it went in, with an empty reserve of 40 BU. Any other item opens the screen.
Open a Biomass Bladder, put the awakened piece in its slot and press Fill. The Bladder moves what the piece can take, 40 BU at most, and nothing else.
Grown from an Organ Bud on Living Substrate: supply two Bone Plates and two Membrane Sheets. Give a plate first, or sneak with an empty hand to choose it.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.awa: Wake a dormant piece in an Awakening Cradle.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.roo: Craft your first Spore Culture: rotten flesh, a red mushroom and wheat seeds, in any arrangement.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.a_c: Hold a Spore Culture in your inventory.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.liv: Use a Spore Culture on exposed ground.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.org: Craft or grow an Organ Bud, a blank that grows into an organ.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.dig: Digest a batch in a Digestive Sac for your first fuel; a full Sac pauses instead of spilling.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.bio: Pour a bucket of biomass into a Biomass Bladder to store it.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.mem: Run a Membrane Rack on Living Substrate with rotten flesh or leather, string and water until it finishes a Membrane Sheet.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.bon: Run a Bone Loom on Living Substrate with a bone and a bucket of biomass until it finishes a Bone Plate.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.bio: Run a Bio-Furnace on Living Substrate with an item to smelt and a bucket of biomass until it finishes a batch.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.lea: Grow a Leaching Pod on Living Substrate over soft ground and let it turn a layer into Leached Rock. Then dig the pit with your bare hands and see the ore in it.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.tun: Grow a Tunnel Root, load it with Root Segments and biomass, and let it cut its first step.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.roo: Steer a Tunnel Root left or right, then walk through the bend in the tunnel it cut.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.cut: Let a Fracture Jaw cut into a Work Bed and Collection Cilia send the cut material through the Item Veins.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.sur: Approve a plan on Surveyed Tissue and let a Structure Grower build a step of it.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.dna: Take a DNA sample from a pig with a Sampling Needle.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.gen: Produce a genetic construct in a DNA Bank from a complete genome.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.roo: Apply a Stairs Construct to a Tunnel Root head and make it a Descending Rootstock.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.wid: Apply a Wider Section Construct to a Rootstock.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.des: Have a Rootstock's minehead cut and build a staircase step on its own.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.sta: Have a Rootstock's minehead finish a staircase section down to its landing.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.min: Have a gallery face of a minehead cut and build a route step on its own.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.sha: Have one minehead find two gallery faces ready to cut at once.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.wid: Have a three-jaw gallery face build a step of the Wider Section.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.pig: Complete the pig genome in a DNA Bank from the samples you gathered.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.pla: Set a Planting Proboscis on Living Substrate beside Cultivation Tissue, give it biomass and a seed by hand, and let it plant the seed. Next, a Harvest Corolla over the same beds cuts the ripe crop.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.har: Give a Harvest Corolla biomass and let it cut a ripe crop from Cultivation Tissue under and around it; bone meal ripens wheat. Next, an Output Mouth under it and Item Veins carry the harvest to a Digestive Sac.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.sup: Let a Digestive Sac finish a batch on food that arrived through an Output Mouth, Item Veins and an Intake Mouth under the Sac, such as a Corolla's wheat. Next, send the biomass back to the organs with a Bladder, a Junction and Biomass Veins.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.aut: Earn the three steps before it: a Planting Proboscis plants, a Harvest Corolla harvests and a Digestive Sac digests the harvest it was sent. Credit goes to the player who placed or last loaded each organ.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.tre: Grow a Capsule Stem into a tree (a chest, two Membrane Sheets and a Spore Culture make the stem; bone meal grows the pods) and put an item in it yourself, at a pod or in the stem's list. A hopper, a Mouth or a pipe does not count. Next, a Shaping Palm that takes its ingredients from storage.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.pal: Give a Shaping Palm Reach and a Mouth, join that Mouth by Item Veins to a chest or a Capsule Tree, press Restock and take a craft made with what the network brought; or let a Palm with Rote finish a cycle on items its Mouth fetched. A craft on your own items, or a route nobody uses, does not count.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.raw: Let a Mineral Gizzard on Living Substrate finish a grind of raw iron, raw gold or raw copper: four dust, a Tailings and a Rock Residue, for biomass and room in its trays. Next, wash the Tailings in a Washing Kidney, and smelt the dust in a Bio-Furnace.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.was: Let a Washing Kidney finish a wash of an Iron, Gold or Copper Tailings of 4 units: water, biomass and room for its dirty water give one more dust and a Tailings of 3 units. Settling dirty water into Rock Residue does not count.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.dus: Let a Bio-Furnace smelt four dust of one metal into an ingot. Smelting a raw item directly is the furnace's old step and does not count.
advancement.infestusfrontier.contact.ore: Earn the three steps before it: a Gizzard grinds a raw metal, a Kidney washes its Tailings and a Bio-Furnace smelts dust into an ingot, in any order. Credit goes to the player who last loaded each organ by hand.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.activ: Place it on Living Substrate. Put in the ingredients of one treatment, by hand or by hopper, with water and biomass from buckets. It starts on its own and takes 20 seconds. The Bowl makes Fusion Binder, Elastic Gel and Rooting Gel too, in 60. Any other item opens the screen.

Fusion Binder and Elastic Gel are ingredients of the other treatments. Capillary Gel grows a Biomass Vein out of a cell of mature Living Substrate, Contractile Fiber an Item Vein, Filter Membrane a Fluid Vein that Sealing Resin then seals. Rooting Gel and Synaptic Gel are made for the crop beds and the nerves that come with the next organs; until then they are kept, not used.
An Organ Bud, two Membrane Sheets and a Bone Plate.
gui.infestusfrontier.vascular_junction.p: Click a face with the Synaptic Probe to cycle it: closed, intake, outlet
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.bioma: A green lumen that carries biomass

Use Capillary Gel on exposed mature Living Substrate. Veins connect biomass stores and organs into a passive network on floors, walls and ceilings. A Junction transfers between loaded endpoints. Veins hold no biomass and do no pumping of their own; loops and branches only establish connections.

Full destinations refuse transfers, leaving biomass at its source. Known vein connections can cross unloaded chunks, but unloaded stores and organs are unavailable. Unknown terrain must load before a connection can be discovered. The probe reports discovery and the 1024-cell network limit. Breaking a vein leaves Dead Tissue; stored biomass stays in the organs.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.item_: Use Contractile Fiber on an exposed cell of mature Living Substrate. An Item Vein holds nothing itself: it joins Mouths into one network, along floors, up walls and around corners. A Mouth set to output sends a store's items through it to the Mouths set to intake that take them.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.septu: Two routes through one cell, unmixed

Use the graft on a vein to create two independent straight passages. Each belongs to its own network; they never join or hold contents. The clicked face shows both lumens and has no passage. The probe turns the crossing; sneak with the probe to read a passage. Seal Fluid Veins before grafting. Breaking it leaves Dead Tissue.
A Membrane Sheet and a Bone Plate make the graft.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.vascu: Carries a vein over a step

Place it in the corner of a one-block step between veins of the same carrier. It connects the two cells as one network, including upside down under a ceiling. It holds nothing and drops off when either supporting cell goes.
Contractile Fiber and a Membrane Sheet make one stitch.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.fluid: Use Filter Membrane on exposed mature Living Substrate, then seal the vein with Sealing Resin. Sealed veins connect compatible liquid endpoints; they own no fluid. A Vascular Junction can draw from or supply the network. Each tank keeps its own liquid; liquids never silently mix. Ordinary Fluid Veins refuse biomass, hot fluids and gases.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.vascu: The pump: intakes, outlets, closed mouths

Place it on Living Substrate. Click a face with the Synaptic Probe to make it an intake, an outlet or closed; the mouth shows it. Every 4 ticks it drains up to 250 mB from each intake, a Bladder, a Sac, a vein or a water source block, into its 1000 mB tank, and pushes as much out of each outlet into a vein, a tank or an organ. It holds one liquid at a time. Any hand opens its screen; sneak with the probe to read it.
An Organ Bud, two Membrane Sheets and a slime ball.
gui.infestusfrontier.vascular_junction.t: One liquid at a time, 1000 mB. Intakes fill it, outlets drain it, 250 mB every 4 ticks.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.mouth: Connect a store to the living workshop

Place a Mouth under a chest or organ. Item Veins and Mouths touching its sides form the network. Intake receives items; output offers them to accepting intakes, highest priority first, rotating equal priorities. Both handles organ ingredients and products. Transfers happen directly between loaded stores. Open the Mouth, or probe its store, to configure it. A Shaping Palm that has Reach uses the Mouth under it the same way, to draw from and send to the network.
One Bud, one hopper and one Membrane Sheet. Nine filter slots allow or deny items. An amount keeps that many in an output's store, or fills an intake's store up to it.
gui.infestusfrontier.mouth.filter.story: Click an item into a slot to list it; click a slot with an empty hand to clear it. An empty filter passes everything.
gui.infestusfrontier.mouth.carried.story: Undelivered items retained after a destination refused execution. Saved here and retried without extracting more.
gui.infestusfrontier.mouth.mode.story: Intake: the network fills the store above. Output: the network takes from it. Both: for an organ, which takes ingredients and gives only products. Closed: neither; items still pass through.
gui.infestusfrontier.mouth.list.story: Allow: only the listed items pass. Deny: everything but them.
gui.infestusfrontier.mouth.amount.story: Intake fills the store up to this many of each item; output leaves this many in it. Shift-click lowers.
gui.infestusfrontier.mouth.priority.stor: Higher-priority intakes are served first. Equal priorities take turns regardless of distance. Shift-click lowers.
Hoppers, mouths and planters leave this many of each kind. A stick raises it by one; after 64 it starts again at 0.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.culti: A crop bed grown from substrate

Use Rooting Gel on an exposed cell of mature Living Substrate. Any crop plants on the bed as on farmland. It holds 1000 mB of water from a bucket or a Fluid Vein; while it has water the crop grows as on wet farmland, and the bed drinks a sip now and then. It plants nothing and harvests nothing.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.seed_: Place it on Living Substrate. It holds four kinds of planting stock, a stack of each, put in by hand, hopper or mouth. A stick raises the reserve by one, from 64 back to 0. Hoppers, mouths and planters take only what a kind has beyond the reserve. Any other item opens the screen, where you take what you like. Breaking it spills the stock.
Leather, a Membrane Sheet and Spore Culture.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.plant: Place it on Living Substrate. Its plot is the nine cells under and around it. Every second it plants one seed on the first empty Cultivation Tissue of the plot, for 5 BU: from its own slot first, then from any chest or Seed Pouch beside it, above the pouch's reserve. Seeds go in by hand, hopper or mouth; biomass by bucket or vein. A seed that cannot stand there costs nothing. Next, a Harvest Corolla over the same beds cuts what ripens.
An Organ Bud, a wooden hoe, Rooting Gel and a Membrane Sheet.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.harve: Cuts the ripe crops around it

Place it on Living Substrate. Its plot is the nine cells under and around it. Every second it cuts one ripe crop of the plot into its four slots, the same drops a hand would get, for 5 BU. It never replants: a Planting Proboscis does. When the drops do not fit, the crop waits. An Output Mouth, a hopper or a vein takes the harvest; nothing goes in by hand. Next, put an Output Mouth under it and run Item Veins to an Intake Mouth under a Digestive Sac, so the wheat feeds the Sac with no hands.
An Organ Bud, an iron hoe and two Membrane Sheets.
entry.infestusfrontier.organ.steward.tex: Hands-free work counts for one player, the organ's steward: whoever placed it or last loaded it by hand (a seed into the Proboscis, food into the Sac). An organ nobody has tended is taken by the first player to open its screen. Standing near it, or opening the screen of an organ that already has a steward, changes nothing. The steward earns the farm milestones while away, on the next login. Breaking the organ forgets its steward.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.compo: Place it on Living Substrate. Four seeds or four leaf blocks and 100 mB of water make one bone meal in 20 seconds. It starts on its own; a hopper or a mouth loads it. What goes to compost cannot also go to the Sac.
A composter, an Organ Bud and a Membrane Sheet.
infestusfrontier.status.lobe.no_organ: No organ to serve: face it at an organ's side
infestusfrontier.status.lobe.serving: Serves the %s: lobe %s of the %s its stage takes
infestusfrontier.status.lobe.idle: Idle: the %s takes %s of this kind at its stage
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.feedi: Place it on a foundation beside an organ; it turns to face it and joins it. Whatever reaches the lobe goes into the organ, which keeps only what its next batch can use. Stand it on a Mouth set to intake and the network feeds the organ. A young organ takes one lobe of each kind, and one more for each stage it grows. Use it to read its state.
An Organ Bud, a Membrane Sheet and a slime ball.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.yield: Place it on a foundation beside an organ; it joins it. It gives what the organ has finished and never its ingredients. Stand it on a Mouth set to output and the network carries the products away. Feeding and Yield Lobes make an organ a small factory: plan where they and their Mouths go.
An Organ Bud, a Membrane Sheet and a Bone Plate.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.tread: Ground that feels who stands on it
Synaptic Gel and a spider eye make the graft.

Use the graft on mature Living Substrate with nothing on top: the cell grows a pad of nerve bulbs, flush with the ground. It is a pressure plate in the ground. Any creature standing on it presses it, as on a stone plate, and it springs back within a second after the last one steps off; items do not press it. Pressed, it powers every block beside and below it, and those pass the power one block on, as any powered block does; the block on top gets a little too. So put it in front of a door, beside the cell the door stands on, and the door opens for whoever walks up. Mobs press it too: a Clenched Door with a receptor outside opens for zombies. Broken, it dies into Dead Tissue.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.senso: An eye that reads how full a block is
An Organ Bud, a comparator and a spider eye.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.fuel_: Use it on an exposed cell of mature Living Substrate: the cell becomes a pad, flush with the ground. It holds one packet, 250 BU, which a Biomass Vein or a Junction keeps topped up (a bucket is more than it holds); a Filter Valve keeps your source's reserve. Once a second it fills the chosen worn awakened pieces of one player standing on it, 10 BU at most, plus a fifth for overhead. Use it to choose the pieces and how full.
Capillary Gel and a Membrane Sheet make the graft.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.senso: Place it against the block to watch: beside it on the floor, or on top of it. Every half second it reads how full that block is, biomass first, then any fluid, then items, as a power of 0 to 15, 1 at least for anything at all; its eye lights up when it reads anything. The power comes out of every other side, as weak redstone and as a comparator value. Put a chest in front and a redstone lamp beside it, and the lamp tells you something is there.
Whether the pad fills this worn piece.
The pad fills each chosen piece up to this share of its capacity.
infestusfrontier.status.filter_valve: Keeps %s mB in the store it faces
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.filte: Place it on a foundation facing a store: a Bladder, a Sac, a tank. Drain the store through the valve with a Junction intake or a bucket on its other sides, and the valve stops it at the reserve. Filling goes through. A stick steps the reserve: none, 250, 500, 1000 up to 16000 mB, then none again. Any other hand reads it.
A Bone Plate, a slime ball and paper.
infestusfrontier.refusal.storage.body_ou: Part of this reservoir is not loaded or is still forming
gui.infestusfrontier.reservoir_cell.body: %s cells in one full box share one tank. It fills from the bottom layer and drains from the top. A whole row or layer grows it, up to 4 on a side; a cell that would leave a gap waits outside with its own biomass.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.reser: Bladders that grow into one tank

A cell holds 4000 BU and stands on a foundation such as Living Substrate, on another cell or on a Vascular Junction. Touching cells that fill a whole box, up to 4 on a side, become one body: the walls between them go, and biomass fills the bottom layer first and drains from the top. Grow it by whole rows and layers; a cell that would leave a gap waits outside with its own biomass. A bucket, vein or junction on any cell reaches the whole body. A broken cell keeps its own share.
A Biomass Bladder, two Bone Plates and two Membrane Sheets. The cell keeps what the Bladder held.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.body.s: One store for the whole stem. Every stem cell opens all of its pods as one list, a bulk pod's one compartment and a Mixed Craw's four counted alike; a pod opens only itself.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.held.s: Every kind the stem holds, its pods counted together, sorted by name. Click to take a stack, click with items in hand to put them in; scroll for more.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.growth: Bone meal on any cell feeds the root. A growth at the first level costs one; each level up costs twice as much, thirty-two at the sixth. A lost cell or pod is regrown first, at its level's cost.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.pod.tr: A Skeletal Graft put here grows the pod a grade: sixteen stacks, then thirty-two. An Elastic Gel put here turns an empty pod into a Mixed Craw for good. Spare items come back when the screen closes; at the last grade a shift-clicked graft is stored like any item.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.pod.fi: This pod alone: click or shift-click to take a stack or put items in. Any stem cell opens the whole stem.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.pod.cr: A Mixed Craw holds four kinds, an eighth of a bulk pod's depth each and half its room in all. A Skeletal Graft put in the well grows it a grade. A Sealing Resin put in the well of an empty Craw turns it into a Larder for good. The change to a Craw cannot be undone.
This Craw alone: four compartments, one kind each. Click or shift-click to take a stack or put items in. Any stem cell opens the whole stem.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.pod.ge: The pod holds items. Empty it before an Elastic Gel can turn it into a Mixed Craw.
Only an empty bulk pod becomes a Mixed Craw.
This pod's saved state is unreadable, so it cannot change.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.pod.re: The Craw holds items. Empty it before a Sealing Resin can turn it into a Larder.
Only an empty Mixed Craw becomes a Larder.
This pod's saved state is unreadable, so it cannot change.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.pod.la: A label must be an item a capsule takes, and a compartment that holds another kind keeps its own label.
Only an empty compartment gives up its label.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.pod.wi: Your cursor must be empty, or hold that kind with room, to withdraw the reserve.
gui.infestusfrontier.item_capsule.pod.la: One kind. A click takes only what the reserve leaves, as a hopper would; the reserve itself comes out through Withdraw. Items go in freely.

The label: the first item the compartment takes, or an item clicked here. It stays when the compartment empties, and the compartment then takes that kind alone. Click here with an empty hand to clear it, while the compartment is empty.
The reserve of this compartment: a count no hopper, Mouth, Item Vein or pipe takes. Click to step up through 0, 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and on to the compartment's limit; shift-click steps down.
Withdraw reserve: takes up to one stack of the reserved part into your cursor. The reserve setting stays as it is; only you at this screen can take what it keeps.
Held is what the compartment has. Kept is the part its reserve protects. Free is what hoppers, Mouths and pipes may take.
A Larder holds three kinds, each with a label and a reserve, at a Craw's depth. A Skeletal Graft put in the well grows it a grade. The change to a Larder cannot be undone.
This Larder alone. Any stem cell opens the whole stem, where a kind's tooltip shows what is held, kept and free.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.item_: A stem that grows pods, each a store of one kind

The advancement Stock in the Tree comes from your own click: put a stack in the stem's list, or in a pod that hangs on a standing stem. A hopper, a Mouth or a pipe is not your hand, a pod that stands on no stem is no tree, and a stack the tree has no room for earns nothing. Next, a Shaping Palm can craft from what the tree holds.

Plant a Capsule Stem on Living Substrate or a ground organ and bone meal it: the stem rises, forks once and grows pods on its trunk, two to four a tier, up to six tiers and sixteen pods. A pod holds one kind of item, eight stacks when young; its face shows the kind and the count. Any stem cell opens the whole stem as one sorted list of kinds, each counted over its pods; a pod opens only itself, a stack in or out and a treatment well; hoppers, pipes and Mouths at the root reach every pod, filling a kind's own pod before an empty one.

At a crafting table, an Infected Log, a chest, two Membrane Sheets and a Spore Culture make a stem. Get the log from a tree your Living Substrate turned (Infected Timber): an oak log or an old Infected Plank is refused. Pods grow; none is crafted. Stems already grown keep their pods and contents.
tooltip.infestusfrontier.larder.label: %s · keeps %s
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.item_: Bone meal on any cell feeds the root. A growth at the first level costs one bone meal; each level up costs twice as much, thirty-two at the sixth. A lost cell or pod is regrown first. Bone meal where nothing fits is kept. A Skeletal Graft, used on a pod or put in its treatment well, grows it a grade: sixteen stacks, then thirty-two.

A broken trunk cell leaves Dead Tissue and orphans the pods above it until bone meal regrows it in place; a broken pod comes out whole with its stock and can be pressed back on the trunk; a broken root, or one dug out from under, kills the stem from the bottom up, each dying cell shedding its pods as items with their contents.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.mixed: A pod that holds four kinds in small amounts

Put one Elastic Gel in the treatment well of an empty pod. It keeps its grade and its place on the stem and becomes a Craw: four compartments, each one kind. Each holds one stack of its kind when young, two at the next grade, four at the last: half a bulk pod's room in all, for the parts and tools you need a few of. A stack is the item's own, so an unstackable tool is 1, 2 or 4. A kind fills its own compartments before it opens an empty one. The Culture Bowl and the Activation Cyst make the gel.

The pod must be empty: a pod that holds anything refuses the gel and says so, and the gel stays in the well. The change cannot be undone and the gel is not returned. A Skeletal Graft grows a Craw as it grows a pod. Broken, carried and pressed back on a trunk cell, a Craw keeps its stock, grade and kind; a pod cannot be placed inside another pod. An empty Craw can become a Larder with Sealing Resin.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.larde: A pod that keeps part of its stock out of reach of automation

Put one Sealing Resin in the treatment well of an empty Mixed Craw. It keeps its grade and its place on the stem and becomes a Larder: three compartments of the Craw's depth, each with a label and a reserve. A Larder has one compartment fewer than a Craw: that room is the price. The first item a compartment takes labels it, or click an item on the label well; the label stays when the compartment empties, and the compartment then takes that kind alone. The Activation Cyst makes the resin.

Step a compartment's reserve with its Keep button: 0, 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and on to its limit. Hoppers, Mouths, Item Veins, pipes and other mods see only what is held above the reserve; items go in freely. When the stock falls to the reserve, the line stops, and when it is refilled the line runs again. A reserve under a Mouth's amount keeps the larger of the two. Each compartment shows held, kept and free; a stem cell's list shows the same in a kind's tooltip.

A click on a compartment takes only the free part. Withdraw reserve takes up to one stack of the kept part into your cursor and leaves the reserve as set. Nothing else does. The pod must be empty to become a Larder; the change cannot be undone and the resin is not returned. Broken or carried, a Larder keeps its stock, labels and reserves.
infestusfrontier.status.network.unavaila: unavailable; topology changed or knowledge limit reached
death.attack.infestusfrontier.spore: %1$s was struck by an Aerocyte Bloom
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.aeroc: A spore crown against flying hostiles

Root it on Living Substrate with clear space above its crown. Feed biomass by bucket or vein. Every two seconds it fires one green pellet at a visible phantom, ghast or blaze within 24 blocks, spending 5 BU. A hit deals two hearts. Walls block shots; players, pets and ground hostiles are safe.

Its 1000 BU tank feeds the shots. Kills collect into eight wells; only overflow falls. Output Mouths and Yield Lobes take the loot. Dry or full, the Bloom rests. Pellets vanish on impact or after two seconds, cannot be recovered, and never load chunks. Ordinary mob defences still apply.
An Organ Bud, a bow, two Bone Plates and a spider eye form its crown.
item.infestusfrontier.mineral_tailings.u: %s units of metal left in it
item.infestusfrontier.mineral_tailings.i: Cannot be smelted or ground again. A Washing Kidney washes a fresh one once. Craft it into Rock Residue to be rid of it.
item.infestusfrontier.mineral_tailings.u: Holds no recoverable metal. It can still be crafted into Rock Residue.
gui.infestusfrontier.mineral_gizzard.wai: The next grind waits until there is room in: %s
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.miner: Three advancements follow this line. Raw Ore to Dust: your Gizzard finishes a grind of raw iron, gold or copper. One More Dust: a Washing Kidney finishes a wash. Dust to Ingot: a Bio-Furnace finishes four dust of one metal into an ingot; a raw item smelted directly does not count. A batch counts for the player who last loaded the organ by hand, even away, and only once it has finished and delivered. A Workshop That Grinds is awarded for all three.

Place it on Living Substrate. Put in raw iron, raw gold or raw copper, by hand or by hopper, and a bucket of biomass. It holds 64 raw items of one kind. Each raw item takes 20 BU and 8 seconds and gives four dust of its metal, one Mineral Tailings and one Rock Residue. Ingots, nuggets, storage blocks, ore blocks and every other ore are refused.

Dust, Tailings and Rock Residue each have a tray of one stack of one kind. A grind starts only when all three have room, so change metals only once the trays are empty. A full tray pauses the Gizzard and its screen marks it Full. Empty the trays by hand, with a Yield Lobe or through an Output Mouth. Nothing is dropped and nothing is deleted.

Two Rock Residue craft into one cobblestone. A Tailings holds the metal the grind left behind: it cannot be smelted or ground again. A Washing Kidney washes a fresh one once for one more dust. Craft any Tailings into Rock Residue to discard it, or keep it.

Smelt dust in a Bio-Furnace: four dust of one metal make one ingot for 40 BU and the furnace's usual time, with the experience of the raw item. Fewer than four wait; extra dust stays and counts toward the next ingot. One raw item through the Gizzard and the furnace makes exactly one ingot, for 60 BU and 24 seconds. Smelted directly it makes the same ingot for 40 BU and 16 seconds, so the line pays in hands-free flow and in dust that keeps.
An Organ Bud, an iron pickaxe, two Bone Plates and two flint.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.fract: Cut a block in place and send it to storage

Three organs, each crafted from an Organ Bud, cut and carry. Put a Fracture Jaw on Living Substrate facing the block to cut, a Work Bed right behind it, and Collection Cilia on a Mouth beside the bed, facing it. Set that Mouth to Output or Both and join it with Item Veins to an Intake Mouth under a chest or capsule. The jaw never moves and never chooses what to cut.

Every 3 seconds the jaw cuts the one block in front of it, as a stone pickaxe would, and puts what that block drops, once, into the Work Bed behind it. A cut costs 10 BU of biomass; the jaw holds two buckets. Fill it by bucket, pipe or a Vascular Junction outlet beside it. All the jaws of a dimension share 8 cuts a tick.

The bed holds nine stacks of cut material. Only a jaw puts items in: hoppers, pipes and veins do not reach it. Open it to take what it holds by hand. When a cut does not fit, the jaw waits and nothing is cut.

Each second the cilia offer up to 16 items from the bed in front of them to the network through the Mouth under them. The Mouths decide what goes where, by their filters and priorities. Only what a far store really took leaves the bed; the rest stays. A sweep that sends something costs 2 BU; the cilia hold one bucket.

The jaw names its reason: no biomass, no Work Bed behind it, a full bed, nothing in front, a block harder than stone grade, a block with an inventory or a piston arm, fluid in the block, a torch, plant, rail or other fragile block touching it, ground not loaded, or no foundation. The cilia name theirs: no biomass, no Mouth under them, the Mouth not set to give, no bed in front, or storage full.

Fix the cause and the organ goes on: add biomass, empty storage or add a store, remove the fragile block, or come back so the ground loads. Nothing drops loose while they wait, and nothing is lost or made twice. Break any of the three with the Surgical Blade and it comes out whole with its biomass, contents and count of work, through unloading, saving and restarting too.
The jaw: an Organ Bud, a stone pickaxe, two Bone Plates and a flint. The bed: an Organ Bud, a chest and two Membrane Sheets.
The cilia: an Organ Bud, two string and a Membrane Sheet.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.surve: Plan a staircase or a gallery and grow its root, treads and lights

Set Surveyed Tissue into the ground at the entrance, facing the way the section goes. Open it to shape a plan, see it drawn in the world, and approve it. Put a Structure Grower on the marker and load it: it builds the approved plan a step at a time. It cuts nothing. Clear each step by hand, with a jaw, or any other way.

A staircase descends one block a step, straight ahead, at most 32 blocks. Each step is a root cell with a tread on it and three clear blocks over the tread. The last step is a landing: a root cell as deep as the staircase, with the same headroom.

A route is a level gallery, at most 64 cells. Each cell is a root cell level with the marker, two clear blocks over it, as in a Tunnel Root's tunnel. It may turn a quarter left or right at up to two cells; the root bends there. Start one from Surveyed Tissue set in a landing's floor.

The marker draws the steps still to build through the ground: amber while a draft, green once approved. It shows only the shape to clear, never the ore. Shift moves a length or a turn by eight. Lit plans hang a torch every 8 steps. The screen shows where the plan ends and what it needs. Approved, the plan no longer changes.

Load Root Segments, stairs and torches by hand, at its screen, or with a hopper. Once a second, when every block of the next step is clear, it grows the root cell, lays the tread and hangs the light, pays for them and moves on. All the growers of a dimension share 4 steps a tick. It never touches a built step again: what you change there stays.

The grower names its reason: no marker or a draft plan, the plan finished, the next step not loaded, fluid or any block in it, no solid ground under its root cell, a creature in the way, no Root Segment, stairs or torch, or no wall to hold the light. It builds nothing until the whole step can be built.

Fix the cause and it goes on: clear the step, fill the ground, step aside, or load stock. Nothing is placed or paid twice. The marker keeps the plan and the steps built, and the grower keeps its stock, through unloading and restarts. Broken with the Surgical Blade, the grower comes out whole; the marker comes out blank and its plan stays behind.
Surveyed Tissue: two Root Segments, a Membrane Sheet and redstone. The grower: an Organ Bud, two Bone Plates and two Root Segments. Treads are any stairs; lights are torches.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.desce: Let a minehead cut, export and build a staircase

A Tunnel Root head with the Stairs mutation is a Descending Rootstock. Set it before an approved staircase and surround it with the organs that do the work, and it becomes a minehead: it orders each cut, step by step, down to the landing. The Rootstock itself cuts, carries and builds nothing.

Facing the way the staircase goes: Surveyed Tissue flush in the ground in front of the Rootstock, facing the same way, with a Structure Grower on it. Right behind the Rootstock a Fracture Jaw facing it, on Living Substrate or a vein, and a Work Bed behind the jaw. Collection Cilia on a Mouth beside the bed, facing it. Every part is an ordinary organ: break one with the Surgical Blade and place it again to rebuild.

The jaw and the cilia draw biomass through their own ports, from a Vascular Junction or a bucket. The cilia's Mouth sends the cut to the Item Vein network: Intake Mouths filtered for raw ore can feed a Mineral Gizzard, others take cobblestone and other spoil into storage. Root Segments, stairs and torches reach the grower from a filtered Intake Mouth under a hopper that points into it.

The Rootstock orders the blocks of the next step only, top down: three blocks of headroom, the tread, then the root cell. The jaw cuts one every 3 seconds as a stone pickaxe would, for 10 BU, into its bed. Once the step is clear the grower lays the root cell and the tread, and the Rootstock counts one step descended. A section descends at most 32 blocks; at its landing the staircase is finished and galleries may open there.

The Rootstock's screen names the part that holds it up; its tooltip gives the reason. The minehead's own: a missing or turned part, a draft or finished plan, unloaded ground, fluid in or next to the step, a loose block on top of it, or no ground under the next root cell. The parts' own: a full Work Bed or no storage taking the cut, no biomass, rock too hard, or no segments or treads.

Fix the cause and it goes on from the same step: empty the storage, supply biomass or stock, put the part back, drain the fluid, mine the loose block, or come back so the ground loads. Each block is cut once and each step built once. The plan, the built steps, every organ's contents and the Rootstock's history stay through breaking and placing again, unloading and restarting.
The cutting organs: a Fracture Jaw and Collection Cilia. The Work Bed and the Mouth come from their own entries.
The plan and the builder: Surveyed Tissue and a Structure Grower.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.minin: Cut level routes from a landing with several faces on one line

When a minehead's staircase reaches its landing, the landing becomes a root junction and the minehead goes on: it orders level galleries cut from there. Each gallery is a route of up to 64 cells with up to two turns, cut by its own face. One minehead works at most four faces at once.

A junction is a root cell where routes meet: the landing, and the last cell of every finished route. Set route Surveyed Tissue flush in the floor right beside the junction, to its left, ahead or to its right, facing away from it: never back the way the root came, so a junction joins at most three routes. A finished route's end is a new junction for the next routes.

Every unfinished route is a working face with its own organs. A Structure Grower stands on its marker. One to three Fracture Jaws stand beside the grower, on its left, its right or behind it, each facing it, with a Work Bed behind each jaw and Collection Cilia on a Mouth facing that bed. The jaws cut what the minehead orders for their face; the grower builds each step once it is clear.

Run one biomass line to every face's jaws and cilia, one Item Vein network from every face's cilia to sorting and storage, and one stock line to every grower. The minehead gives its faces cuts in turn: a face that has just been given one waits until each other face that can cut has had one. A face that cannot cut never holds up the others.

The Rootstock's screen counts its faces at work and paused; its tooltip names each face's step, or the part that holds it up and why. A face whose jaws run dry, whose bed fills with no storage taking the cut, or whose grower runs out of stock pauses alone and goes on from the same step once you supply it. Every cut lands in a bed or in storage, once.

Set a route to 3x3 at its Surveyed Tissue. A wide route is three across and three high, a root cell under each column. Its face needs a Rootstock with the Wider Section mutation and all three jaws; otherwise it pauses and says which is missing. A wide step is twelve cuts to a narrow step's three: four times the biomass, the spoil and the bed space, and three segments instead of one. A 1x2 route still works from any Rootstock.

A route runs at most 64 cells with two turns; a wide route may not double back onto itself. A minehead works at most four unfinished routes and looks at no more than thirteen routes in all: past either, every face pauses until you take a marker out. The whole walk from the landing must be loaded; an unloaded junction or face pauses the galleries, and they go on when it loads, also after a restart.
gui.infestusfrontier.washing_kidney.wait: The next wash or settle waits until there is room in: %s
gui.infestusfrontier.washing_kidney.room: Every tray and the dirty tank have room
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.washi: Wash Tailings for one more dust

The advancement One More Dust comes from a wash that finishes: a Tailings of 4 units, water, biomass and room for the dust and the dirty water. Settling dirty water into Rock Residue does not count. It counts for the player who last loaded the Kidney by hand, even away. With Raw Ore to Dust and Dust to Ingot it makes A Workshop That Grinds.

Place it on Living Substrate. Put in Iron, Gold or Copper Tailings of 4 units, by hand or by hopper, a bucket of biomass and a bucket of water. It holds 64 Tailings of one kind. A wash takes one Tailings, 250 mB of clean water and 30 BU, and after 8 seconds gives one dust of its metal and a Tailings of 3 units. The 250 mB of water turns dirty and stays in the Kidney. It needs no power and no genome.

A Tailings is washed once. The washed Tailings of 3 units is refused by the Kidney, as are another Tailings, a raw item and a dust. Keep it, or craft it into Rock Residue. One raw item gives four dust ground and one washed: five dust, one ingot and one dust over for the next washed item.

Dirty water has no bucket, vein or pipe and nothing else can take it out. The Kidney holds 1000 mB. When the tank cannot take 250 mB more, it settles instead: 1000 mB of dirty water and 20 BU become one Rock Residue after 20 seconds. Four washes and one settle cost 52 seconds, 1000 mB of water and 140 BU for four dust and one Rock Residue. The Kidney is slower than the Gizzard: a line that washes wants a second Kidney or accepts unwashed stock.

A full dust, Tailings or Rock Residue tray, or a full dirty tank with no room to settle, pauses the Kidney and its screen marks it Full. Empty the trays by hand, with a Yield Lobe or through an Output Mouth, and it resumes. Nothing is dropped or deleted, and no waste can be turned back into water, ore or dust.
An Organ Bud, two Membrane Sheets, sand and a glass bottle.
infestusfrontier.refusal.processing.palm: No room for the result or a remainder. Make room in your inventory
This Palm has no Living Substrate under it. It keeps its grid and crafts nothing
gui.infestusfrontier.shaping_palm.result: Take it to craft once, shift-click to craft as many as the grid holds. Ingredients and remainders stay in the grid when you close the screen.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.shapi: Shaping Palm
A crafting table that keeps its grid
Crafted From Stock

The advancement Crafted From Stock comes from a craft made with an item the Palm's Mouth fetched from a chest or a Capsule Tree: Restock fills the grid, or a Mouth under a Palm with Rote delivers, and you take the craft or Store it. Your own items, a hopper's items and a route nobody uses do not count. The Palm's steward is whoever placed it or last loaded it by hand; a Palm nobody tended is taken by the first player to open it. A finished cycle on fetched items counts for the steward, even away.

Place it on Living Substrate. Any hand opens its screen: a three by three grid and a result well, laid out as at a crafting table. Put ingredients in and close the screen; they are still there when you come back. Click the result to craft once, or shift-click to craft as many as the grid holds. It runs the crafting recipes of the game and of other mods, with their own inputs, outputs and remainders. Crafting by hand costs no biomass and no time.
What a craft takes

A craft takes one of each filled cell and nothing more. A remainder, such as a bucket, a bottle or a bowl, goes back to its emptied cell, or into your inventory when it cannot. If the result or a remainder has no room, the craft is refused and nothing changes. Two players at one Palm take turns: each craft uses the grid as it is then.
What it keeps

Broken, a Palm comes out whole with its grid, and placed again it has it back. Without Living Substrate under it, it keeps its grid and crafts nothing. Hoppers, pipes and Lobes cannot reach a Palm until it has Rote, and a Palm without Rote repeats nothing by itself.
An Organ Bud, a crafting table, two Membrane Sheets and a Bone Plate.

infestusfrontier.status.palm.stored: Crafted once and sent %s items to the network
A Contractile Fiber used on the Palm gives it Reach: the Mouth under it becomes its door to the Item Vein network.
The Mouth under the Palm is its only door to storage. It must take (Intake or Both) for Restock and give (Output or Both) for Return and Store. Join it by Item Veins to a Mouth on a chest or a Capsule Tree. The lips under the Palm show it: an arrow up for takes, down for gives, both for both, none when closed. Use the probe on the Palm to open the Mouth.
gui.infestusfrontier.shaping_palm.restoc: Tops each filled cell up to a full stack with the same item from the output Mouths on the network. A Larder's reserve stays in the Larder. It crafts nothing.
gui.infestusfrontier.shaping_palm.return: Sends the grid to the intake Mouths on the network. What no Mouth takes stays in its cell.
Crafts once and sends the result to the network, not your inventory. Refused whole when no Mouth takes it.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.shapi: Reach and the Mouth

Use a Contractile Fiber on the Palm: it gains Reach, and the fiber is spent. The Palm reaches storage through one door only, the Mouth under it, which also serves as its foundation. Join that Mouth by Item Veins to a Mouth under a chest or a Capsule Tree, a Craw or a Larder pod. The Palm keeps no position and searches for nothing: the Item Vein network is the only link. Use the Synaptic Probe on the Palm to open its Mouth. Broken, a Palm keeps Reach.
Restock, Return, Store

Restock tops every filled cell up to a stack with the same item from the output Mouths of the network. Return sends the grid to its intake Mouths. Store crafts once and sends the result there. Restock needs the Mouth under the Palm set to Intake or Both; Return and Store need Output or Both. The Mouth's filter, amount and priority apply, and so do each far Mouth's. A Larder keeps its reserve, so a Restock takes only the free part. Each button is one pass that you choose: nothing repeats and nothing is made for you. If the route is broken, a store is unloaded, short or full, the screen says so and nothing moves.
Where to see it

The default demo has two Palms with a Mouth under each. One draws from a Capsule Tree with bulk, Craw and Larder pods, the other from a chest, each over a visible Item Vein route. Both craft iron bars into a chest on their own. Break a vein and no more ingots come; the Palm finishes what it already holds. Put the vein back and it works again. In the Rote row, a plank line works on its own. North of those rows, four Palms show each Mouth symbol.

gui.infestusfrontier.shaping_palm.status: No Rote
A Synaptic Gel used on a Palm with Reach gives it Rote.
No pattern
Fill the grid with one recipe and press Select.
Working %s%%
A cycle is under way. It takes 2 seconds and its ingredients and 10 BU are already spent.
Ready
Everything is in place. The next cycle starts as soon as the server admits it.
Missing items
A grid cell lacks the item the pattern holds there, or holds another. Feed it with a Lobe or a hopper, or restock through its Mouth.
Needs 10 BU
A cycle spends 10 BU when it starts. Feed biomass to the Palm with a bucket, a Mouth or a Junction.
Tray full
The tray has no room for the result and every remainder. Take them with a Yield Lobe, a hopper or by hand.
Recipe changed
The recipe or its result is no longer what Select recorded. Nothing is lost. Select again, or put the recipe back.
No supply
The grid needs a restock and the Mouth under the Palm cannot reach the network: it is closed, set to Output, or the network is rebuilding or busy. The Palm waits and asks again.
No foundation
A Palm works only on an organ foundation such as Living Substrate.
Unreadable
The Palm's saved data could not be read. It keeps the bytes and does nothing.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.shapi: Palm on a Mouth
A Capsule Tree above, a chest below: Item Veins join each Mouth to the Mouth under a Palm. The lips on the Palm screen show that Mouth: arrow up takes, down gives, both arrows both.
The Rote tray
The tray under Select: the first well holds what a cycle makes, here a cake; the three marked wells take the remainders.
Rote

Use a Synaptic Gel on a Palm that has Reach: it gains Rote, and the gel is spent. Fill the grid with one crafting recipe and press Select. The Palm records each cell's item, the recipe and its result, and refuses a recipe whose result depends on the inputs (dyeing, repair, maps, fireworks), a grid that makes nothing, and a recipe with more than 3 kinds of remainder. It holds one pattern, and Select again replaces it only between cycles.
The cycle

When the grid holds the pattern, the tray has room for the result and every remainder, and the Palm holds 10 BU, it takes one of each ingredient and the biomass, and 2 seconds later puts the result and the remainders in its tray. Feed it biomass with a bucket, a Mouth or a Junction. While a cycle runs, the hand closes over its plate. If the recipe changes, or something is missing or full, the screen says why and nothing is lost. A cycle in the middle of a save carries on where it was, and its products appear once.
Lobes and the Mouth

A Feeding Lobe or a hopper fills a grid cell only with the item the pattern holds there. A Yield Lobe or a hopper takes the result and the remainders from the tray, never the grid. A Mouth under the Palm set to Output or Both also carries the tray's products out over the Item Veins. After each finished cycle the Palm restocks its pattern cells once through the Mouth under it; a Larder keeps its reserve, and a network that cannot be reached leaves the restock owed and the Palm says so. A network that has none of the item leaves the Palm short until you feed it or press Restock. A Palm still crafts by hand as before. The Iron Bars Factory entry shows a Palm at the end of a whole line.
entry.infestusfrontier.circulation.iron_: Raw iron to iron bars, with no hand in it
Pink: items. Dust skips the Kidney to the furnace. Residue and washed Tailings go to the waste chest. Green: biomass. Blue: water.

A working line stands in the default demo, south of the exhibit rows at x 0 to 31, z -22 to -15. A Larder of raw iron feeds a Mineral Gizzard. A Washing Kidney washes its Tailings. A Bio-Furnace smelts the dust into ingots. A Shaping Palm with Rote crafts the ingots into iron bars in a chest. You bring the raw iron and the biomass. The line digs and makes neither.

Every hop is a Mouth with a filter. Larder, Mouth, Feeding Lobe, Gizzard. Its Yield Lobe sends dust to the furnace, Tailings to the Kidney and Rock Residue to the waste chest. The Kidney sends its dust to the furnace and its washed Tailings and residue to the waste chest. The furnace sends ingots to the Palm. The Palm sends bars to the output chest. The Kidney's Mouth has priority 1, so Tailings are washed before they are thrown away. Every hop is a Mouth and the Item Veins between them: no hidden link carries anything.

The Larder holds 18 raw iron and keeps 3. The other 15 run through the line. Each raw iron is 4 dust, and its washed Tailings gives 1 more: 75 dust, which is 18 ingots and 3 dust left. 18 ingots are three crafts of 6 ingots, and a craft is 16 bars: 48 bars. The run spends 1,560 BU: 300 to grind, 450 to wash, 60 to settle, 720 to smelt and 30 in the Palm. It draws 3,750 mB of water: 3,000 settle into Rock Residue and 750 stay dirty in the Kidney. It leaves 15 washed Tailings and 18 Rock Residue. A first-stage furnace sets the pace: 16 s an ingot, about five minutes.

Raw iron is yours: mine it, with Fortune if you like, and put it in the Larder. The line makes none. Biomass: a Reservoir holds 4,000 BU and a Junction pushes it into a biomass vein under the organs. Each organ draws what it needs into its own tank, up to 1,000 BU, the furnace 2,000. Fill the Reservoir with Biomass Buckets, or join its Junction to a farm. Water: three source blocks in a stone pool. A Junction drinks from the middle one and the pool fills itself again. Dirty water never leaves the Kidney.

The Larder keeps 3 raw iron. The line never takes them; take them yourself at its screen. The waste chest takes washed Tailings and Rock Residue. When it is full the Gizzard says Full and waits; empty it and the line goes on. A full output chest fills the Palm's tray at 64 bars, and the Palm says Tray full. To cut a supply, use the Synaptic Probe on a Junction face: two clicks close an intake and a third opens it. The organs use what their tanks hold, then wait. Read the tanks and the Palm's status line.

Culture Bowl: Spore Culture and Organ Buds. Bone Loom: Bone Plates. Membrane Rack: Membrane Sheets. Activation Cyst: Capillary Gel for biomass veins, Contractile Fiber for item veins and Reach, Synaptic Gel for Rote, Elastic Gel and Sealing Resin. A Biomass Bladder becomes the Reservoir cell. You need two Junctions, eleven Mouths, four Feeding Lobes and four Yield Lobes. A Capsule Stem grows a pod: Elastic Gel makes it a Craw, Sealing Resin a Larder. The Gizzard, Kidney, Bio-Furnace and Palm have their own entries.

Vanilla's own recipe: six iron ingots in two rows of three make 16 iron bars. Use a Contractile Fiber, then a Synaptic Gel on a Palm. Put six ingots in its top two rows and press Select. The Palm then takes ingots only into those six cells and spends 10 BU and 2 seconds a craft.
